tools.name: lookup_phone
tools.description: Identify the country and mobile operator of a phone number and list the top-up offers available for it. Free. The operator is DETECTED from the number range and is a guess: MVNOs (Tesco Mobile, Giff Gaff, Lebara, Voxi, Sky…) resolve to the host network they ride on. Read the detected brand back to t

tools.name: list_offers
tools.description: Browse purchasable offers: mobile top-ups, travel eSIMs, prepaid bills, or international payment corridors (bank / mobile money / UPI) for a country. Free. Prices shown are indicative; the quote fixes them.

tools.name: quote
tools.description: Lock a price (10 minutes) for one purchase. Returns quoteId, exact USDC price and what will be delivered. Free. ALWAYS show the human the price and the recipient before buying.

tools.name: create_pay_link
tools.description: Create a checkout link a HUMAN pays from their own Algorand wallet (Pera). Use this when you have no wallet, or when the person should approve and pay themselves: they open the link, see the exact price, sign in their wallet, and the result (the eSIM QR code, or the top-up confirmation) appears on t

tools.name: buy
tools.description: Get the x402 payment challenge for a quote. This hosted server holds no wallet, so it does NOT spend your money: it returns the exact amount, asset, payTo address and facilitator for you to pay from your own Algorand wallet, then you POST the quote again with your payment signature. Requires prior h

tools.name: quote_vouchers
tools.description: Lock a price (10 minutes) for a BATCH of travel eSIMs paid in one payment: N claim links, one per person, for a group trip, a conference delegation or event giveaways. Each eSIM is bought when its link is claimed (the person opens it on their phone and installs the QR), and links nobody claims withi

tools.name: voucher_batch
tools.description: A paid voucher batch: every claim link, which have been claimed and delivered, the expiry, and any refund for unclaimed links. The batchId is the only handle on the links — keep it, and hand each person their own link privately (whoever opens a link first gets that eSIM).

tools.name: order_status
tools.description: Check an order. Poll every ~3 s until `terminal` is true: delivered (confirmation + signed receipt), refunded (refund txid + signed receipt) or refund_failed.

tools.name: verify_receipt
tools.description: Verify an ed25519-signed receipt: the signature, and — unless you pass onChain:false — both txids against an Algorand indexer. Give it an orderId to check one of this service's own orders, or a receipt object to check ANY receipt in this format, including one issued by another server.

tools.name: fx
tools.description: Indicative USDC → local-currency rate at our sale price, with an estimate for an amount. The quote is the binding price.

tools.name: ledger
tools.description: Public delivery ledger: totals, delivered-or-refunded %, volume, countries, recent orders.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: buy · Private data: create_pay_link, buy, quote_vouchers · Public sink: create_pay_link, buy, quote_vouchers · Destructive: verify_receipt.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: buy · Private data: create_pay_link, buy, quote_vouchers · Public sink: create_pay_link, buy, quote_vouchers · Destructive: verify_receipt

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "buy" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
